10.1b — 3-Button Jam: Rapid Prototype

A great pitch on paper can still feel boring or awkward the second your fingers touch the keys. Today is Rapid Prototyping: build a rough greybox version where all three buttons work inside a plain test scene. No custom sprite art, no title screen, no music — only proving that pressing your three buttons feels responsive and fun.

Why Greybox? Speed Over Pretty (~15 min) ~15 min

If you spend two days drawing pixel animations before wiring movement and jumping, any redesign hurts because you already sunk hours into art. Professional jam teams prototype with squares, circles, and basic solid colors for one reason: if an idea fails a prototype test today, throwing away three squares costs nothing.

What Belongs in Today's PrototypeWhat Waits Until After Playtesting
All 3 Input.GetKeyDown() / Input.GetKey() verbs working reliably Final sprites, animations, backgrounds, particle effects
Your riskiest movement, physics, or timing interaction Title menu, credits screen, multiple themed levels
Reused patterns (triggers, Instantiate(), cooldown timers, TextMeshPro debug score) Sound effects and screen shake polish
In the Editor + Code: Wire All 3 Buttons & Reuse Patterns (~45 min) ~45 min
  1. Build the Riskiest Part First: write only the scripts needed for your main object and its 3 inputs (for example: rb.AddForceY(), rotation/thrust, lane snapping, or spawning via Instantiate()).
  2. Borrow What You Know: reuse every Semester 1 habit cleanly — [SerializeField] tuning fields in the Inspector, cooldownTimer -= Time.deltaTime rates, CompareTag() triggers, and OnCollisionEnter2D() resets.
  3. Put One Target / Obstacle in the Room: give your 3 buttons something to dodge, catch, shoot, or climb over so you can feel whether timing and distances click.
  4. Run the 5-Second Fun Check: press Play with ONLY your 3 keys for 60 seconds. Ask yourself brutally: Is just moving and pressing these three buttons engaging even with ugly squares? If not, tune speed/gravityScale/jumpForce right now — or pivot before investing another day!
Do not build level 1 before fixing button feel. A jam game lives or dies on its core 3-second loop (press → react → physics/reward). Tune your movement curves and cooldowns in one flat sandbox BEFORE designing obstacles around them.

Socratic: Prototyping Honesty

  1. After building your greybox prototype today, which of your three buttons felt the crispest right away, and which one felt clunky, slow, or confusing?
  2. What exact thing from Units 1–8 did you reuse inside today's scripts (cooldownTimer, CompareTag(), Instantiate(), SetParent(), wayPoints), and what part had to be written fresh?
  3. What happened during your 60-second test that surprised you — did your original pitch need a number tweak, a rule simplification, or a backup idea?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Play a greybox Unity scene where all 3 input buttons trigger distinct visible actions
  • Interact with at least one placeholder obstacle, target, or timer without throwing errors
  • Confirm the 3-button controls obey the strict 3-input limit from 10.1a
  • Commit and push your working prototype cleanly
